chunks: And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Bazanṭī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, he said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who dies while he has an umm al-walad, and he has a child from her: is it permissible for a man to marry her?

He said: I was informed that ʿAlī عليه السلام gave instruction regarding the mothers of children with whom he had relations: whoever among them had a child, she is from the share of her child; and whoever did not have a child, then she is free.
And only those among them who had a child were made from the share of their child so that they would not marry except with the permission of their family.

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: a female slave who has borne a child to her master
key_terms.بِإِذْنِ أَهْلِهَا: with the permission of her family
key_terms.نَصِيبِ وَلَدِهَا: the allotted share of her child

ai.seo_question: Can an umm al-walad be married after the death of her master according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal status of an umm al-walad after the death of her master and whether she may marry. It reports that Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled that one who had borne a child remained attached to her child's share, while one without a child was free, with the stated purpose of regulating her marriage through the permission of her family.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3509 - In a narration from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Bazanti, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, he said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (as), about a man who dies and leaves behind an Umm al-Walad (a female slave who bore him a child) and has a child from her. Can another man marry her?

Imam (as) said: "I was informed that Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), instructed regarding the Umm al-Walad women he had relations with:
'Whoever among them has borne a child, she becomes the share of her child. And whoever has not borne a child, she is set free.'
And those who had children were assigned to their children to ensure that they would not marry except with the permission of their family."
